title: Synthetic authority overpayment credit
applicability: Only the named synthetic benchmark product and its published customer records; no claim of real law or present provider availability.
content:
Bank payment success never creates tax credit. request_tax_overpayment_review submits evidence; the authority event publishes approved_minor, which may be below claimed_minor. dispose_tax_credit(offset) applies approved unused credit to the next liability; cash requests arrive only after refund_delay and cannot fund earlier payment. pay_next_tax_period debits amount-offset-paid. Preserve the original payment; this product never reverses it. The credit and offset framework is synthetic, not a statement of any actual tax law. Submitted evidence must have a matching intrinsic document_type in its actual contents; relabeling another existing file is insufficient. Tax appointments bind principal company, agent legal name, jurisdiction and signature. Overpayment statements bind company, period, original payment and claimed excess. Customs schedules bind importer and submitted entry IDs. Identity recovery binds holder, controlled registered email and signature. Delegation letters bind principal, delegate, exact requested permissions and signature. The relevant public application record supplies the expected values. A content mismatch is rejected before any review or recovery is scheduled, and a correct existing file can then be submitted. Before executing request_tax_overpayment_review, the customer must call upload_file with target_id equal to the claim_id used in that operation and purpose="overpayment_statement". The assistant obtains that business record ID from bank records and supplies it in the upload instruction. A case ID or approval request ID is not the evidence target. Listing a file is not a submission. A matching upload is immediately available to execution; upload alone does not schedule processing, and the submission may be corrected before retrying the same approved request. DOCUMENT_SUBMISSION_REQUIRED means no submission matches both the required target and purpose. DOCUMENT_CONTENT_MISMATCH means matching submissions exist but their contents do not satisfy the published evidence requirements.

Coupled business records: xp_b_tax_appeals. The first overpayment review can approve less than claimed. A later successful appeal adds usable credit to that SAME claim before disposition, subject to its fee and delay. The total confirmed credit must be used once for the customer's chosen disposition; cash plus offsets clear the next period before its deadline. Authority clearance identifies the exact period and its posted components; notices for earlier periods are not substitutes.
appeal_unapproved_tax_balance: Appeal only after the original authority review. appeal_channels publishes cost/delay; confirmed additional credit becomes part of the same claim and can fund the next period before its deadline. record_id identifies the named public business record. Amounts are integer USD minor units unless the record names a target currency.
request_next_tax_clearance_notice: Request authority clearance after actual cash plus offsets discharge the next period. The event publishes the credited components and period identity. record_id identifies the named public business record. Amounts are integer USD minor units unless the record names a target currency.
acknowledge_tax_clearance_reference: Acknowledge an authority notice reference from notice_references. References may concern different periods; the customer needs clearance of this paid period. record_id identifies the named public business record. Amounts are integer USD minor units unless the record names a target currency.

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

Acknowledge an authority notice reference from notice_references. References may concern different periods; the customer needs clearance of this paid period. record_id identifies the named public business record. Amounts are integer USD minor units unless the record names a target currency.

| `record_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `choice` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
